narr: Isolated to scattered showers and storms developed along the border with southeastern Virginia in the afternoon hours. The storms then propagated south and southwest during the evening hours. Several reports of flooding were observed, along with a few wind damage reports.
ev: Mount Gilead Church Road was closed due to flooding between US highway 64 and Sugar Lake Road.
Henry Oldham Road was closed in several locations due to flash flooding.
Flash flooding was reported at the intersection of Reedy Fork Parkway and Blue Stem Drive with cars stranded in flood waters.
Alamance County emergency management reported up to eight water rescues in downtown Burlington.
The road was closed due to flash flooding at the intersection of West Webb Avenue and South Fisher Street in Burlington.
The USGS stream gage along Reedy Fork near Gibsonville rose above moderate flood stage to 14 feet. The gage rose 13 feet in 3 hours.
The USGS stream gage along North Buffalo Creek at Westover Terrace rose above minor flood stage of 10 ft.
There was a water rescue at Sycamore Glen Road and Reedy Fork Parkway after a vehicle stalled in flood waters.
A portion of Oakley Road was washed out due to high flowing water.
The public reported high water flowing over Pearson Road where it crosses South Fork Little River.
